authors: Max van Drunen Tomás Dodds Hannes Cools Theresa Josephine Seipp
raw_title: EU Audience Measurement Regulation: Implications for the Media’s Democratic Role
raw_abstract: New EU legislation aims to regulate audience measurement systems for the first time. With these rules, EU policymakers primarily seek to increase transparency, enabling media organisations to better understand the allocation and pricing of advertising revenue on platforms. However, as a long history of research in journalism studies shows, audience measurement systems also play an important role in editorial decision-making. This commentary draws on legal and journalism studies literature to offer a first exploration of the way new EU regulation of audience measurement systems could impact the media’s democratic function. It finds that the regulations’ focus on transparency may exacerbate power inequalities within the media system and between media and platforms, while their financial rationale neglects the impact audience measurement systems have on editorial decision-making. The commentary identifies ways to mitigate these challenges and closes by briefly highlighting new research opportunities that these upcoming EU regulations open up by making more data available on audience measurement systems.
